plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for Nokia (Alcatel-Lucent) Wavence microwave radios (enterprise PEN 637, OPTICSIM-RADIO-TRS-COMMON-MIB). Besides standard IF-MIB interface traffic and uptime, it reports local and remote transmit power and main-receiver input level per radio interface.
name: Transmission

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes received over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCInOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCOutOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: wavence_local_tx_power_dbm
metrics.description: Local radio transmit power in dBm from OPTICSIM-RADIO-TRS-COMMON-MIB analogueMeasuresLocalTxPower (1.3.6.1.4.1.637.54.1.10.1.1.4.1.2). The Integer32 is in 0.1 dBm units (range -1000..1000) and is divided by 10 in the collector.

metrics.name: wavence_local_rx_power_dbm
metrics.description: Local main-receiver input level in dBm from OPTICSIM-RADIO-TRS-COMMON-MIB analogueMeasuresLocalRxMainPower (1.3.6.1.4.1.637.54.1.10.1.1.4.1.3). The Integer32 is in 0.1 dBm units (range -1000..0) and is divided by 10 in the collector.

metrics.name: wavence_remote_tx_power_dbm
metrics.description: Remote radio transmit power in dBm from OPTICSIM-RADIO-TRS-COMMON-MIB analogueMeasuresRemoteTxPower (1.3.6.1.4.1.637.54.1.10.1.1.4.1.6). The Integer32 is in 0.1 dBm units (range -1000..1000) and is divided by 10 in the collector.

metrics.name: wavence_remote_rx_power_dbm
metrics.description: Remote main-receiver input level in dBm from OPTICSIM-RADIO-TRS-COMMON-MIB analogueMeasuresRemoteRxMainPower (1.3.6.1.4.1.637.54.1.10.1.1.4.1.7). The Integer32 is in 0.1 dBm units (range -1000..0) and is divided by 10 in the collector.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
